headline: An Indian parliamentary committee chairman said India's security policy is not shaped by social media pressure, replying to Elon Musk's criticism of the resistance to Starlink.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: The Hindu's text matches the headline, but it is one politician's statement that gives no detail of the alleged threats.
importance_line: The reply bears first on people in India waiting for satellite internet, whose access depends on security clearance, then on the government and Indian telecom rivals, then on Starlink; it is one politician's statement that names no specific threat, and by Reuters' report in our 11 Oct edition the approvals are still pending.
summary: The Hindu reports that Nishikant Dubey, a Bharatiya Janata Party MP who leads the parliament's standing committee on information technology, said on Sunday 11 Oct that India's security policy is not made under pressure from social media, replying to Elon Musk's criticism of the resistance to Starlink, his satellite internet service, entering India; Dubey said the defence and home ministries and investigators had raised concerns about "dangerous games", claimed similar worries were raised in 2013-14 without saying what the threats were, and told Musk to "provide connections to the poor in your own country" first. It is the latest turn in the Musk and Starlink row our 9, 10 and 11 Oct 2026 editions followed, the last of them Reuters, as carried by The Business Times, on Musk's 10 Oct pledge on X to price Starlink affordably in India.
notes: Read The Hindu's short article in full. Follow-up of 1011:C05-02 (our 11 Oct 2026 edition). What is new today: the reply of the committee chairman; The Hindu does not say which Musk remark he answers, so the summary names the row, not one post.
